'''Rajendra Singh (Rajju Bhaiya)''' (29 January 1922 – 14 July 2003), was the fourth ''[[Sarsanghchalak]]'' (Supreme Leader) of the [[Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh]] (RSS), a [[right-wing politics|right-wing]] [[Hindutva]] [[paramilitary]] organisation. He was supreme leader of that organisation between 1994 and 2000. A physicist by profession, he was a professor and head of the Department of Physics at the [[University of Allahabad]] but left the post and joined the RSS full-time in 1966.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |title=RSS conclave ends with a resolve to transcend caste divisions in Hindu society |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/rss-conclave-ends-with-a-resolve-to-transcend-caste-divisions-in-hindu-society/articleshow/46590342.cms |work=[[The Economic Times]] |pages=}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Islam |first1=Shamsul |title=Religious Dimensions of Indian Nationalism: A Study of RSS |date=2006 |publisher=Anamika Pub & Distributors |isbn=9788174952363 |page=36 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iaQjbO8SN48C&q=Rajendra+Singh+(RSS)+Sarsanghchalaks&pg=PA36 |access-date=18 August 2018}}</ref>

==Early life==
Rajendra Singh was born on 29 January 1922, in the village of Banail, located in the [[Bulandshahr district]], [[United Provinces of Agra and Oudh|United Provinces]]. He was born into a [[Tomar (Rajput clan)|Tomar Rajput]] family, to parents Jwala Devi and Balbir Pratap Singh. His father was an engineer in the [[Shahjahanpur]].<ref name="krishna" /><ref>{{cite book |last1=Krant |first1=Madan Lal Verma |title=Sarfaroshi Ki Tamanna (Part-1) |publisher=Praveen Prakashan |year=1998 |location=[[New Delhi]] |page=7 |language=hi |chapter=Ashirvachan |oclc=468022633 |quote=मेरे पिताजी सन् 1921-22 के लगभग शाहजहाँपुर में इंजीनियर थे....(ह०) राजेन्द्र सिंह (सरसंघचालक, राष्ट्रीय स्वयंसेवक संघ) [My father was posted as Engineer at Shahjahanpur in near about 1921-22....(Sd) Rajendra Singh, Sarsanghchalak, R.S.S.]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2003-07-25|title=Rajendra Singh|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/rajendra-singh-36818.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210611161928/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/rajendra-singh-36818.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 June 2021|access-date=2020-08-07|website=The Independent|language=en}}</ref>

Rajendra Singh completed his [[Matriculation examination|matriculation]] in [[Unnao]].<ref name="tribune23">{{cite news |date=14 July 2003 |title=From N-physicist to RSS chief |url=http://www.tribuneindia.com/2003/20030715/main3.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080713054351/http://www.tribuneindia.com/2003/20030715/main3.htm |archive-date=13 July 2008 |access-date=6 December 2012 |work=[[The Tribune (India)|The Tribune]] |location=New Delhi}}</ref> He subsequently attended the [[Modern School (New Delhi)|Modern School in New Delhi]] for a brief period before transferring to [[St. Joseph's College, Nainital|St. Joseph's College in Nainital]]. He later pursued higher education at the [[University of Allahabad]], where he earned [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]], [[Master of Science|MSc]], and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degrees.<ref name="krishna">{{cite web |title=Rajju Bhaiyya as I know Him |url=http://www.krishnavirendra.org/lifesktech.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140127142722/http://www.krishnavirendra.org/lifesktech.htm |archive-date=27 January 2014 |access-date=6 December 2012 |website=krishnavirendra.org}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Singh was acknowledged as an exceptionally brilliant student by [[C. V. Raman]], the Indian [[physicist]] and [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel Prize]]-winner, when he was his examiner in MSc. He also offered Singh a fellowship for advanced research in nuclear physics.<ref name=tribune23/><ref>{{cite book |title=Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh: National Upsurge|first=M. G. |last=Chitkara|page=357|publisher=APH Publishers |year=2004 |isbn=9788176484657 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ifuxzl9NM5sC&pg=PA357}}</ref>

He joined [[University of Allahabad|Allahabad University]] after majoring in Physics to teach [[spectroscopy]].<ref name="books.google.com">{{cite book |last=Leon |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Leon |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vLwOck15eboC&pg=PA150 |title=Conflict between India and Pakistan: An Encyclopedia |publisher=[[ABC-Clio|ABC-CLIO Inc]] |year=1998 |isbn=9781576077122 |page=150}}</ref> He taught at the university for several years, where later he was appointed head of the Department of Physics.<ref name=tribune23 /> Singh was also considered an expert in [[nuclear physics]] which was very rare those days in India.<ref name="rediff22">{{cite news |date=14 July 2003 |title=Rajju Bhaiyya was a father figure to Parivar |url=http://www.rediff.com/news/2003/jul/14rajju1.htm |work=[[Rediff.com]]}}</ref> He was a very popular teacher of the subject, using simple and clear concepts.<ref name="tribune23" />

==Association with the RSS==
Singh was active in the [[Quit India Movement]] of 1942 and it was during this time that he came in contact with the RSS.<ref name=tribune23 /><ref name=rediff22 /> The Sangh influenced his life thereafter. He resigned from his university post in 1966 and offered full-time services to the RSS as a ''pracharak''.<ref name=tribune23 /><ref name=rediff22 />

Beginning in [[Uttar Pradesh]], Singh progressed to be the ''Sarkaryavaha'' (General Secretary) in the 1980s.<ref name=tribune23/> On 11 March 1994, [[Madhukar Dattatraya Deoras]], the third ''[[Sarsanghchalak]]'' of the RSS, became the first head of the organisation to step down voluntarily, citing health reasons. He appointed Singh as his successor.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theprint.in/politics/3rd-rss-chief-balasaheb-deoras-organiser-strategic-thinker-who-made-swayamsevaks-introspect/779754/ |title=3rd RSS chief Balasaheb Deoras: Organiser, strategic thinker who made swayamsevaks 'introspect' |first=Arun |last=Anand |date=11 December 2021 |website=[[ThePrint]]}}</ref><ref name="Rediff21">{{cite news |date=15 July 2003 |title=He was the final word for the Parivar |url=http://in.rediff.com/news/2003/jul/15guest.htm |work=[[Rediff.com]]}}</ref> While in Uttar Pradesh, Singh worked with [[Lal Bahadur Shastri]], [[Chandra Shekhar]] and [[V. P. Singh]].<ref name="Rediff21" />

In 1998, Indian politics underwent a significant shift when the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] (BJP), closely affiliated with the RSS, emerged as the largest party in the [[Parliament of India|Indian parliament]]. The BJP led the [[National Democratic Alliance]] (NDA) coalition government, with [[Atal Bihari Vajpayee]] serving as [[Prime Minister of India|prime minister]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Chaturvedi |first=Rakesh |date=17 August 2018 |title=There would have been no NDA government in 1998 had Atal Bihari Vajpayee not been the face of BJP |url=https://economictimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/there-would-have-been-no-nda-government-in-1998-had-atal-bihari-vajpayee-not-been-the-face-of-bjp/articleshow/65433250.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190303214523/https://economictimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/there-would-have-been-no-nda-government-in-1998-had-atal-bihari-vajpayee-not-been-the-face-of-bjp/articleshow/65433250.cms |archive-date=3 March 2019 |website=[[The Economic Times]]}}</ref> This marked the first instance of a central government in India being explicitly associated with the ideology of [[Hindutva]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Johnson |first1=Matthew |title=Conservatism and Ideology |last2=Garnett |first2=Mark |author-link2=Mark Garnett |last3=Walker |first3=David M |publisher=[[Routledge]] |year=2017 |isbn=9781317528999}}</ref> However, the Vajpayee government's inability to implement key ideological objectives of the Sangh–primarily due to the constraints of coalition politics and Vajpayee’s moderate stance—led to dissatisfaction and criticism from the organisation.<ref name=":1" />

He gave up the post of ''Sarsanghchalak'' on account of his failing health in February 2000 and nominated [[K. S. Sudarshan]] as his successor.<ref name=tribune23/>

==Ideology and views==
Singh once remarked "Official documents refer to the [''[[sic]]''] 'composite culture', but ours is certainly not a composite culture. Culture is not wearing of clothes or speaking languages. In a very fundamental sense, this country has a unique cultural oneness. No country, if it has to survive, can have compartments. All this shows that changes are needed in the Constitution. A constitution more suited to the ethos and genius of this country should be adopted in the future".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Noorani |first=A. G. |author-link=A. G. Noorani |date=7 July 2019 |title=India's fascist challenge |url=https://frontline.thehindu.com/the-nation/fascist-challenge/article28259898.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210728164554/https://frontline.thehindu.com/the-nation/fascist-challenge/article28259898.ece |archive-date=28 July 2021 |website=[[Frontline (magazine)|Frontline]]}}</ref>

In 1988, Singh praised [[Nathuram Godse]], the [[Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi|assassin]] of [[Mahatma Gandhi]], for his commitment to the concept of [[Akhand Bharat]], stating "His intentions were good but he used wrong methods".<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 January 2017 |title=Why India's Hindu hardliners want to sideline Mahatma Gandhi |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-38794202 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170130114153/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-38794202 |archive-date=30 January 2017 |website=[[BBC]]}}</ref> However, in 1997, in a rally in which Vajpayee was present, Singh called Gandhi "among the sons of [[Bharat Mata]]", adding "He is held in reverence by the society though not decorated by the government with [[Bharat Ratna]]", in an attempt to win support from Gandhi loyalists in the Indian electorate.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Noorani |first=A. G. |author-link=A. G. Noorani |title=The RSS and the BJP: A Division of Labour |publisher=[[LeftWord Books]] |year=2000 |isbn=9788187496137}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Noorani |first=A. G. |author-link=A. G. Noorani |date=24 July 2016 |title=The RSS and Gandhi: A Necessary Backstory |url=https://thewire.in/article/books/the-rss-and-gandhi-2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210216171128/https://thewire.in/article/books/the-rss-and-gandhi-2 |archive-date=16 February 2021 |website=[[The Wire (India)|The Wire]]}}</ref>

In 1999, Singh attacked liberals and progressives as a "class of bastards which tries to implant an alien culture in our land".<ref>{{Cite book |first=Walden |last=Bello |author-link=Walden Bello |year=2019 |title=Counterrevolution: The Global Rise of the Far Right |publisher=Practical Action Publishing |isbn=9781788530521 |page=81}}</ref>

==Death==
Singh died on 14 July 2003 at Kaushik Ashram in [[Pune]], [[Maharashtra]], where he had been residing following his retirement.<ref name=tribune23/> The following day, he was cremated at the Vaikunth Crematorium in Pune. His funeral was attended by prominent figures such as his successor, ''Sarsanghchalak'' [[K. S. Sudarshan]], alongside senior BJP leaders including then prime minister Vajpayee, then [[Deputy Prime Minister of India|deputy prime minister]] [[L. K. Advani]], and then [[Vice President of India|vice president]] [[Bhairon Singh Shekhawat]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.rediff.com/news/2003/jul/15rajju.htm| title = Rajju Bhaiyya cremated in Pune - Rediff.com}}</ref>
